_meta.task: chunk contains PII (binary; drives contains_pii and so retrieval exclusion)
_meta.provenance: Corpus chunks are produced by src.data_processing.ingest_pipeline.extract_and_chunk over data/sample_deal/*.txt; each row pins the chunk text by sha1 so the runner refuses to score stale labels after a chunking change. Labelled by hand by Claude (the implementing agent) reading every chunk; synthetic rows were written by the same agent, are marked syn-*, and use obviously fake people and numbers. Rows marked borderline are excluded from scoring for that label (counted separately). Split: corpus by document (dev = board deck, credit agreement, customer contracts, QoE report; test = the other five documents) so no document contributes to both; synthetic rows alternate dev/test. Single annotator - no inter-annotator agreement was measured.
_meta.guideline: Positive: data about an identifiable natural person that is private - government IDs (SSN, passport, driver licence), date of birth, home address, personal phone/email, personal bank details, health, background-check or census data (pii_kind=identifier) - or the pay of a specific named or identifiable individual (pii_kind=compensation). Negative: names and titles in a business capacity (signature blocks, presenters), corporate addresses, accounts and EINs, invoice or case numbers, aggregate pools and expense lines, and text that talks about personal data without containing any.
_meta.policy_note: pii_kind=compensation follows the existing detector's stated policy (it flags salary data). The corpus's only genuine PII is named-executive compensation in the employment schedule, which the golden QA set also asks about (comp_05, mh_06); see results.md for the retrieval-damage trade-off.
